explanation: Split links into an even-position chain and an odd-position chain while walking the original list. Append each successive node to its matching chain, then join the even tail to the saved odd head. Relative order and original node identities are preserved.
timeComplexity: O(n) Each node is classified or rewired once.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Only the two chain heads/tails and traversal pointers are retained.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The two pointers successively retain exactly the even-indexed and odd-indexed original nodes, in original order. Separating their links and joining the even tail to the saved odd head creates the required concatenation without introducing new result nodes.
walkthrough: For [10,20,30,40,50], the even positions contain [10,30,50] and the odd positions [20,40]. Joining those chains returns [10,30,50,20,40].
edgeCases: One or two nodes need little or no rewiring.
The final odd tail must terminate rather than retain a stale link.
